title.en: Volume 144 Biographies 69: Lai, Tian, Hou, Cui, Yan

sentences.zh: ◎來田侯崔嚴來瑱，邠州永壽人。

translations.literal: ◎ Lai, Tian, Hou, Cui, and Yan: Lai Zhen was a man of Yongshou in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Biographies of Lai, Tian, Hou, Cui, and Yan. Lai Zhen was a native of Yongshou in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 父曜，奮行間，開元末，持節磧西副大使、四鎮節度使，著名西邊，終右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yao was valiant in martial exploits; at the end of the Kaiyuan era he held the insignia as Deputy Commissioner of the Western Regions and Military Governor of the Four Garrisons, was famed on the western frontier, and ended as Grand General of the Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao had distinguished himself in arms; late in the Kaiyuan reign he served with imperial credentials as deputy commissioner of the Western Regions and military governor of the Four Garrisons, won renown on the frontier, and died as Grand General of the Right Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 瑱略知收，尚名節，崖然有大誌。

translations.literal: Zhen had some knowledge of revenue administration, esteemed reputation and integrity, and stood aloof with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knew something of fiscal administration, prized honor and integrity, and carried himself with stern dignity and high ambition.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，從四鎮任劇職，累遷殿中侍御史、伊西北庭行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served in the Four Garrisons in strenuous posts and was successively promoted to Censor within the Palace and Military Affairs Secretary of Yixi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao period he held demanding posts with the Four Garrisons and rose in turn to palace censor and military affairs secretary for Yixi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 詔舉智謀果決、才堪統眾者，拾遺張鎬薦瑱能斷大事，有禦侮才，擢潁川太守，充招討使。

translations.literal: An edict called for men of resourceful resolve fit to command armies; Remonstrance Official Zhang Hao recommended that Zhen could decide great affairs and had talent to repel insult; he was promoted to Administrator of Yingchuan and made Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne sought men of decisive counsel able to lead troops, Remonstrance Official Zhang Hao urged that Zhen could settle weighty matters and repel invasion; he was made prefect of Yingchuan and appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會母喪免，以孝聞。

translations.literal: He happened to be dismissed on account of his mother's mourning and became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office to mourn and won a reputation for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，張垍薦之，興塊次，拜汝南太守。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Zhang Ke again recommended him; he was reinstated from mourning and concurrently appointed Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: After An Lushan rose in rebellion, Zhang Ke recommended him again; recalled from mourning, he was named prefect of Runan.

sentences.zh: 未行，改潁川。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was reassigned to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, his appointment was changed to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 賊攻潁川，方積粟多，瑱完埤自如，手射賊，皆應弦仆。

translations.literal: When rebels attacked Yingchuan, grain had just been stored in great quantity; Zhen repaired the ramparts as if unperturbed, shot rebels by hand, and all fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels besieged Yingchuan just as the granaries were full; Zhen calmly strengthened the walls, drew his bow himself, and every shaft he loosed dropped an enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊使降將畢思琛招之，父故將也，拜城下，泣且吊，瑱不應，前後俘殺甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the surrendered general Bi Sichen to summon him—an old officer of his father's—who bowed below the wall weeping and offering condolences; Zhen did not respond, and before and after captured and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the defector Bi Sichen, once his father's officer, to parley beneath the walls with tears and condolences; Zhen ignored him and in repeated sorties took and slew a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，目為「來嚼鐵」。

translations.literal: The rebels feared him and called him by the eye-name "Lai Chews Iron."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came to fear him and nicknamed him "Lai the Iron-Biter."

sentences.zh: 以功就加防禦使、河南淮南遊弈逐要招討使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was thereupon additionally made Defense Commissioner, Pacification Commissioner for the vital circuit of Henan, Huainan, and the roaming patrol forces.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was further made defense commissioner and pacification commissioner over the Henan–Huainan patrol and frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 徙山南東道節度使代魯炅，會嗣號王巨表炅方固守，乃還瑱故官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit in place of Lu Jiong; it happened that the Prince of Sihao, Wang Ju, reported that Jiong was still holding fast, and so Zhen was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to military governor of Shannan East to replace Lu Jiong, but when Prince Sihao Wang Ju reported that Jiong was still holding his ground, Zhen was returned to his former command.

sentences.zh: 賊圍南陽急，瑱與魏仲犀合兵救之，不勝，人情恟懼，瑱能撫訓士，舉動安重，賊不得侵。

translations.literal: Rebels pressed Nanyang urgently; Zhen joined forces with Wei Zhongxi to rescue it but did not prevail; popular feeling was alarmed and fearful, yet Zhen could comfort and train the troops, his bearing calm and weighty, and the rebels could not encroach.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels tightened their siege of Nanyang, Zhen marched with Wei Zhongxi to relieve the city but failed to break through; though panic spread, he steadied and disciplined his men, and his calm bearing kept the enemy from pressing further gains.

sentences.zh: 改淮南西道節度。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Governor of Huainan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as military governor of Huainan West.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，封潁國公，食二百戶。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying and granted an income of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern and western capitals were recovered, he was created Duke of Ying with a fief income of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，徙河西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan he was transferred to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he was ordered to the Hexi command.

sentences.zh: 未行，王師敗於相州，詔拜陜虢節度，兼潼關防禦團練鎮守使。

translations.literal: Before he departed, the imperial army was defeated at Xiang Prefecture; he was ordered appointed Military Governor of Shan-Guo and concurrently Defense and Training Commissioner guarding Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, the court army was routed at Xiangzhou; he was named military governor of Shanzhou and Guozhou and put in charge of Tong Pass defense and training.

sentences.zh: 明年，襄州部將張維瑾等殺其使史翙，徙瑱山南東道襄、鄧、均、房、金、商、隨、郢、復十州節度使。

translations.literal: The next year, the subordinate generals of Xiang Prefecture, Zhang Weijin and others, killed their commissioner Shi Hui; Zhen was transferred to be Military Governor of the ten prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, and Fu in Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Xiangzhou officers led by Zhang Weijin murdered their commissioner Shi Hui, Zhen was made military governor of ten prefectures—Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, and Fu—on the Shannan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 既至，維瑾降。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Weijin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Zhang Weijin submitted.

sentences.zh: 上元二年春，破史思明餘黨於魯山，俘賊渠，又戰汝州，獲馬、牛、橐駝，凡兩戰，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Shangyuan he defeated the remnant band of Shi Siming at Lushan, captured rebel chiefs, and again fought at Ru Prefecture, obtaining horses, cattle, and camels; in two battles he beheaded enemies to the number of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 761 he routed Shi Siming's remnants at Lushan, took rebel leaders prisoner, and fought again at Ruzhou, seizing horses, cattle, and camels; in two engagements he claimed ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔瑱還，瑱安襄、漢，士亦宜其政，因諷眾留己，而外示行；

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered Zhen to return; Zhen had brought peace to Xiang and Han, and the troops also approved his governance, so he prompted the masses to keep him while outwardly showing that he would depart;
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court recalled him; having settled Xiang and Han to the troops' satisfaction, he quietly urged the men to keep him in place while pretending to obey the summons;

sentences.zh: 至鄧，復詔歸鎮。

translations.literal: when he reached Deng, another edict ordered him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: but when he reached Deng, a new edict sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞其謀，惡之，呂諲、王仲昇等皆言「瑱得士心，不可以留』，乃改山南東道襄、鄧、唐、復、隨、郢六州節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong heard of his scheme and detested it; Lü Yin, Wang Zhongsheng, and others all said, "Zhen has won the hearts of the troops and must not be kept," and so he was changed to Military Governor of the six prefectures Xiang, Deng, Tang, Fu, Sui, and Ying in Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong learned of the maneuver and took offense; Lü Yin, Wang Zhongsheng, and others argued, "Zhen has won the army's loyalty and must not be left in place," so his command was reduced to six prefectures on the Shannan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄而仲昇與賊戰申州，為賊禽。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongsheng fought rebels at Shen Prefecture and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Zhongsheng fought the rebels at Shenzhou and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，仲昇被圍，而江陵呂諲病，瑱顧望不即救，及師出，仲昇已沒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongsheng was besieged, Lü Yin at Jiangling was ill; Zhen looked on hesitantly and did not rescue at once, and by the time his army marched out, Zhongsheng had perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongsheng had first been surrounded, Lü Yin at Jiangling lay ill and Zhen delayed his relief; by the time his columns moved, Zhongsheng was already dead.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬裴奰表其狀，且言：「瑱善謀而勇，恐後難制，即除之，可一戰禽也。」

translations.literal: Military Affairs Secretary Pei Yi memorialized the circumstances and moreover said: "Zhen is skilled in planning and brave; I fear he will later be hard to control—if he is removed at once, he can be captured in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: His military affairs secretary Pei Yi reported the affair and urged: "Zhen is resourceful and bold; if he is not removed now he may prove uncontrollable—strike promptly and he can be taken in one fight."

sentences.zh: 帝頗謂然，遂改瑱淮西申、安、蘄、黃、光、沔兼河南陳、豫、許、鄭、汴、曹、宋、穎、泗十五州節度以寵之，陰奪其權，加奰襄、鄧等七州防禦使代瑱。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely considered it so and thereupon changed Zhen to Military Governor of the fifteen prefectures of Huai West—Shen, An, Qi, Huang, Guang, and Mian—and concurrently Henan—Chen, Yu, Xu, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Song, Ying, and Si—to honor him, while secretly stripping his power and promoting Yi to Defense Commissioner of the seven prefectures Xiang, Deng, and others in place of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely agreed and, ostensibly to honor him, transferred Zhen to a grand fifteen-prefecture command spanning Huai West and Henan while secretly curtailing his power by making Pei Yi defense commissioner of seven prefectures including Xiang and Deng in his stead.

sentences.zh: 瑱懼，釋言「淮西無糧，須麥收可上道」，又諷眾固留。

translations.literal: Zhen was afraid and pleaded that "Huai West has no grain and one must wait for the wheat harvest before taking the road," and again prompted the masses to detain him firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Zhen pleaded, "Huai West lacks grain and I cannot march until the wheat harvest," and again stirred the troops to keep him where he was.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，復授襄州節度、奉義軍渭北兵馬使；

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong acceded, he was again granted Military Governor of Xiang Prefecture and Military Commissioner of the Fengyi Army north of the Wei;
translations.idiomatic: After Daizong came to the throne, Zhen was again made military governor of Xiangzhou and commander of the Fengyi army north of the Wei;

sentences.zh: 密詔奰圖之。

translations.literal: a secret edict ordered Yi to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: while a secret order set Pei Yi to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 奰自均州率眾浮漢下。

translations.literal: Yi led his troops from Jun Prefecture down the Han by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi led his force from Junzhou down the Han River by boat.

sentences.zh: 會日入，候者白瑱，瑱與帳下謀，其副薛南陽曰：「公奉詔留鎮，而奰以兵脅代，是無名也。

translations.literal: As the sun set, scouts reported to Zhen; Zhen consulted with his staff, and his deputy Xue Nanyang said: "Your Lordship holds the command by imperial order to remain on guard, yet Yi uses troops to coerce replacement—this has no proper name.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset scouts warned Zhen, who consulted his staff; his deputy Xue Nanyang said, "You hold this post by imperial command, yet Pei Yi comes with an army to displace you—that is an unjust act.

sentences.zh: 奰智勇非公敵，而眾心不附。

translations.literal: Yi's wisdom and courage are not a match for Your Lordship's, and the hearts of the masses do not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: He is no match for you in wit or valor, and the men do not follow him.

sentences.zh: 彼若乘我不虞，縱火夜攻，誠可憂也。

translations.literal: If he should take advantage of our lack of precaution and set fires in a night attack, it would truly be worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: If he catches us off guard with a night assault and fire attack, that would be grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 若須明，則破之必矣。」

translations.literal: If we must fight in daylight, then breaking him is certain.
translations.idiomatic: But meet him in open daylight and you are sure to break him."

sentences.zh: 明日，奰督軍五千陣谷水北，瑱以兵迎之，呼其軍，告曰：「爾何事來？」

translations.literal: The next day Yi marshaled five thousand troops north of the Gu River; Zhen met him with troops, called out to his army, and announced: "For what affair have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Pei Yi drew up five thousand men north of the Gu River; Zhen advanced to meet him and called across to the ranks, "What brings you here?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「公不受命，故中丞伐罪。」

translations.literal: They replied: "Your Lordship did not accept the order, so the Vice Censor is punishing the offense."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "You refused the transfer, so the vice censor has come to punish your offense."

sentences.zh: 瑱曰：「詔還鎮此州。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "The edict orders me to return and guard this prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "The edict orders me to remain and guard this prefecture."

sentences.zh: 乃以詔書示之。

translations.literal: He then displayed the edict to them.
translations.idiomatic: He showed them the edict.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「偽也。

translations.literal: All said: "It is forged.
translations.idiomatic: They cried, "It is a forgery.

sentences.zh: 吾千里討賊，豈空歸邪？」

translations.literal: We have come a thousand li to punish rebels—shall we return empty?
translations.idiomatic: We marched a thousand li to punish a rebel—do you think we will go home empty-handed?"

sentences.zh: 爭射之，瑱走旗下。

translations.literal: They vied to shoot at him, and Zhen ran beneath his banners.
translations.idiomatic: They loosed a volley at him, and Zhen dashed beneath his standard.

sentences.zh: 薛南陽曰：「請公勒兵勿戰。」

translations.literal: Xue Nanyang said: "I beg Your Lordship to restrain the troops and not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Nanyang said, "Hold the line, my lord—do not engage yet."

sentences.zh: 乃以三百騎為奇兵，旁萬山，出其背夾擊之，其眾幾盡，奰脫身走，至申口，禽之，送京師。

translations.literal: He then took three hundred horsemen as a surprise force, flanking along Mount Wan, and struck from behind in a pincer; their host was nearly annihilated; Yi escaped by himself, was captured at Shenkou, and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent three hundred horsemen by a hidden route around Mount Wan to strike from the rear; Pei Yi's army was nearly destroyed, Yi fled alone, was seized at Shenkou, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑱因入朝謝罪，帝待之無疑，拜兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，充山陵使。

translations.literal: Zhen thereupon entered court to apologize; the Emperor received him without suspicion, appointed him Minister of War, Associate Director of the Secretariat with Court Session Privileges, and made him Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then went to court to apologize; the emperor received him without mistrust, made him minister of war and chief councilor, and appointed him commissioner for the imperial tomb works.

sentences.zh: 是時，程元振居中用事，疾瑱，乃告與巫祝言不順。

translations.literal: At that time Cheng Yuanzhen held power at court and resented Zhen; he reported that Zhen had spoken disloyally with shamans and diviners.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen then dominated the court, hated Zhen, and accused him of disloyal dealings with sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 會王仲昇歸，又言由瑱與賊合，故陷賊。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Zhongsheng returned and again said that because Zhen had joined with the rebels, he had therefore fallen into rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhongsheng returned from captivity he added that Zhen had colluded with the rebels and deliberately left him to be taken.

sentences.zh: 帝積怒，遂下詔削除官爵，貶播川尉，員外置。

translations.literal: The Emperor's accumulated anger burst forth; he thereupon issued an edict stripping rank and titles, demoting him to Assistant Magistrate of Bo Prefecture, with supernumerary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath boiled over; an edict stripped his titles and banished him as assistant magistrate of Bozhou on a supernumerary posting.

sentences.zh: 及鄠，賜死，籍其家。

translations.literal: When he reached E, he was granted death, and his household property was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: At E Prefecture he was ordered to take his own life, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 瑱之死，門下客散去，掩屍於坎，校書郎殷亮獨後至，哭屍側，為備棺衾以葬。

translations.literal: At Zhen's death his retainers scattered; the corpse was covered in a pit; Collator Yin Liang alone came afterward, wept beside the corpse, and prepared coffin and shroud for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen died his clients fled, leaving the body in a shallow grave; only collator Yin Liang came later, wept beside the corpse, and provided coffin and shroud for burial.

sentences.zh: 帝徐悟元振誣，以它罪流溱州。

translations.literal: The Emperor gradually realized Yuanzhen's slander and banished him to Qin Prefecture on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor slowly realized he had been deceived and banished Yuanzhen to Qinzhou on another charge.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑱行軍司馬龐充以兵二千戍河南，至汝，聞瑱死，乃還襲襄州，別將李昭禦之，走房陵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhen's Military Affairs Secretary Pang Chong garrisoned Henan with two thousand troops; reaching Ru, he heard of Zhen's death and returned to attack Xiang Prefecture; the subordinate general Li Zhao resisted him, and he fled to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhen's secretary Pang Chong had been stationed in Henan with two thousand men; at Ruzhou he learned of Zhen's death, marched back to seize Xiangzhou, was checked by subordinate Li Zhao, and fled toward Fangling.

sentences.zh: 昭與薛南陽、梁崇義不相臣，崇義殺昭，帝以崇義為節度使代瑱。

translations.literal: Zhao, Xue Nanyang, and Liang Chongyi would not submit to one another; Chongyi killed Zhao, and the Emperor made Chongyi Military Governor in Zhen's place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Xue Nanyang, and Liang Chongyi refused to obey one another; Chongyi killed Zhao, and the throne made him military governor in Zhen's stead.

sentences.zh: 既而為瑱立祠，四時致饗，避瑱聽事不處，哀祈禮葬，詔可。

translations.literal: Thereafter he built a shrine for Zhen, offered seasonal sacrifices, avoided occupying Zhen's audience hall, and tearfully petitioned for a proper burial—the edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He later erected a shrine to Zhen with seasonal offerings, refused to sit in Zhen's hall of audience, and tearfully petitioned for honorable burial, which the court granted.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，追復官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde his offices and titles were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 his rank and titles were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 裴奰者，始以蔭為京兆司錄參軍。

translations.literal: As for Pei Yi, he first entered office by yin privilege as Recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi had first entered office through hereditary privilege as recorder of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑱鎮陜州，引為判官，移襄州，又為行軍司馬，遇之厚。

translations.literal: When Zhen governed Shan Prefecture he brought him in as aide; when transferred to Xiang Prefecture he again made him Military Affairs Secretary and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen governed Shanzhou he took Yi on as aide; at Xiangzhou he made him military secretary and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及瑱私漢上，奰欲得其處，故背瑱言狀，帝倚以圖瑱。

translations.literal: When Zhen privately held the Han region, Yi wished to obtain his post and therefore turned against Zhen in his reports; the Emperor relied on him to plot against Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen clung to his command on the Han, Yi coveted his post, turned informer against him, and won the emperor's trust for the plot to remove him.

sentences.zh: 而性輕褊少謀，師興，給用無節。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was frivolous, narrow, and short on planning; when the army marched, supplies were expended without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: But he was rash, petty, and shortsighted; once his campaign began, he spent supplies without restraint.

sentences.zh: 及敗，有詔流費州，至藍田，賜死。

translations.literal: When he was defeated, an edict banished him to Fei Prefecture; at Lantian he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat he was banished to Feizhou and ordered to die at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 田神功，冀州南宮人。

translations.literal: Tian Shengong—Tian Shengong was a man of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shengong was a native of Nangong in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，為縣史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he was a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao period he served as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 會天下兵興，賊署為平盧兵馬使，率眾歸朝，從李忠臣收滄、德，攻相州，拒杏園。

translations.literal: When warfare arose throughout the realm, the rebels appointed him Military Commissioner of Pinglu; he led his troops back to the court, followed Li Zhongchen in recovering Cang and De, attacked Xiang Prefecture, and held Xingyuan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion spread, the rebels made him Pinglu military commissioner; he then led his men back to the Tang side, followed Li Zhongchen in recovering Cangzhou and Dezhou, fought at Xiangzhou, and held Xingyuan Garden.

sentences.zh: 後守陳留，戰不勝，與許叔冀降於史思明。

translations.literal: Later he defended Chenliu, was defeated in battle, and with Xu Shuji surrendered to Shi Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Later, defending Chenliu, he was beaten and surrendered with Xu Shuji to Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 思明使與南德信、劉從諫南略江淮，神功襲德信，斬之，從諫脫身走，乃並將其兵。

translations.literal: Siming sent him with Nan Dexin and Liu Congjian to campaign south into Jianghuai; Shengong surprised Dexin, beheaded him, Congjian escaped by himself, and he then took command of all their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent him south with Nan Dexin and Liu Congjian to overrun Jianghuai; Shengong ambushed Dexin and killed him, and when Congjian fled he absorbed both armies.

sentences.zh: 詔拜鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him minister of diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 襲敬釭鄆州，不克。

translations.literal: He attacked Jing Gang at Yan Prefecture but did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Jing Gang at Yanzhou but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 劉展反，鄧景山引神功助討，自淄青濟淮，眾不整，入揚州，遂大掠居人貲產，發屋剔窖，殺商胡波斯數千人。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhan rebelled, Deng Jingshan brought in Shengong to assist in the suppression; he crossed from Ziqing over the Huai, his troops were not in order, entered Yang Prefecture, and thereupon plundered the residents' property on a great scale, tearing open houses and digging out cellars, killing several thousand Sogdian and Persian merchants.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan rebelled, Deng Jingshan called on Shengong; marching from Ziqing across the Huai in disorder, he entered Yangzhou and looted the city—breaking into houses, emptying storerooms, and slaughtering thousands of Sogdian and Persian merchants.

sentences.zh: 俄而禽展送京師，遷淄青節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he captured Zhan and sent him to the capital, and was transferred to be Military Governor of Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon captured Zhan and sent him to the capital, and was made military governor of Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 會侯希逸入青州，更徙兗鄆。

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Xiyi entered Qing Prefecture, and he was further transferred to Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Xiyi took Qingzhou, his command was shifted to Yanzhou and Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 時賊圍宋州急，李光弼奏神功往救，賊解去。

translations.literal: At that time rebels were pressing Song Prefecture urgently; Li Guangbi memorialized that Shengong should go to rescue it, and the rebels lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were pressing Songzhou hard; Li Guangbi urged that Shengong relieve the city, and the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 又破法子營，復攻敬釭，降之。

translations.literal: He again defeated Fa Zi's camp, again attacked Jing Gang, and received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Fa Zi's camp, attacked Jing Gang again, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 朝義聞，乃奔下博。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi heard of it, he fled to Xiabo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi, hearing this, fled to Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 進封信都郡王，徙河南節度、汴宋八州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Prince of Xindu and transferred to Military Governor of Henan and Observation Commissioner of the eight prefectures of Bian and Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to prince of Xindu and made military governor of Henan and observer of the eight Bian-Song prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年來朝，加檢校尚書右僕射，詔宰相百官送至省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali he came to court; he was additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and an edict ordered the chief ministers and all officials to escort him to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In 767 he came to court and was made acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; the chief ministers and the whole bureaucracy were ordered to escort him to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 又判左僕射，知省事，加太子太師，還軍。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrent Left Vice Director, directed routine business, was additionally made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and returned to his army.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as left vice director in charge of routine business, was named grand preceptor of the heir apparent, and returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 神功事母孝。

translations.literal: Shengong was filial toward his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shengong was devoted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 始，嘗倨驕自如，見光弼待官屬鈞禮，乃折節謙損。

translations.literal: At first he had been haughty and proud as he pleased; when he saw Guangbi treat his subordinates with balanced courtesy, he then restrained himself and became modest.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been insufferably proud, but after watching Li Guangbi treat his staff with measured courtesy he learned to humble himself.

sentences.zh: 既寢疾，宋之將吏為禳祈報恩。

translations.literal: Once he fell ill in bed, the generals and officials of Song offered prayers of expiation to repay his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the officers of Song offered prayers for his recovery in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 八年，自力入朝，卒，代宗為徹樂，贈司徒，詔其弟曹州刺史神玉知汴州留事，賻絹千匹、布五百端，百官吊喪，賜屏風茵褥，飯千桑門追福。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court by his own strength, then died; Emperor Daizong had music withdrawn for him, posthumously made him Minister of Education, ordered his younger brother Shenyu, Administrator of Cao Prefecture, to handle Bian Prefecture affairs as acting commissioner, granted one thousand bolts of silk and five hundred bolts of cloth as funeral gifts, had all officials mourn, bestowed screens and bedding, and fed a thousand monks for merit on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he dragged himself to court and died; Daizong suspended court music, posthumously made him minister of education, left Bianzhou affairs to his brother Shenyu, prefect of Cao, granted a thousand bolts of silk and five hundred of cloth, ordered the bureaucracy to mourn, gave screens and bedding, and fed a thousand monks for his soul.

sentences.zh: 至德後，節度使不兼宰相者，惟神功恩禮最篤。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, among military governors who did not concurrently serve as chief ministers, only Shengong received the most earnest favor and ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide period, of the military governors who were not also chief ministers, none received court favor so lavish as Shengong.

sentences.zh: 神玉終汴宋節度留後。

translations.literal: Shenyu ended as Acting Military Governor of Bian and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyu ended his career as acting military governor of Bian and Song.

sentences.zh: 侯希逸，營州人。

translations.literal: Hou Xiyi—Hou Xiyi was a man of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi was a native of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，豐下銳上。

translations.literal: He was seven chi tall, full in the lower body and sharp in the upper.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet, broad below and sharp-featured above.

sentences.zh: 天寶末為州裨將，守保定城。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was a deputy general of the prefecture, guarding Baoding City.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he was a deputy commander of the prefecture, holding Baoding City.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使中人韓朝敭傳命，希逸斬以徇。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent the eunuch Han Chaoyang to deliver orders; Xiyi beheaded him and displayed the head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled he sent the eunuch Han Chaoyang with orders; Xiyi executed him and exposed the head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 祿山又以親將徐歸道為節度使，希逸率兵與安東都護王玄誌斬之，遣使上聞，詔拜玄誌平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Lushan again made his trusted general Xu Guidao Military Governor; Xiyi led troops with Protector-General of Andong Wang Xuanzhi to behead him, sent envoys to report upward, and an edict appointed Xuanzhi Military Governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan then installed his favorite Xu Guidao as military governor; Xiyi joined Andong protector Wang Xuanzhi in killing him, reported to the court, and Xuanzhi was appointed military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 玄誌卒，副將李正己殺其子，共推希逸，有詔就拜節度使，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Xuanzhi died, the deputy general Li Zhengji killed his son; together they pushed Xiyi forward, and an edict appointed him on the spot as Military Governor, concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzhi died, deputy Li Zhengji killed his son and the army acclaimed Xiyi; he was appointed military governor on the spot and made grand censor as well.

sentences.zh: 與賊確，數有功。

translations.literal: He clashed with the rebels repeatedly and had many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebels again and again with repeated success.

sentences.zh: 然孤軍無援，又為奚侵掠，乃拔其軍二萬，浮海入青州據之，平盧遂陷。

translations.literal: Yet as a lone army without support, and again harried by Xi raids, he drew off twenty thousand of his troops, crossed the sea into Qing Prefecture and held it, and Pinglu thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: But isolated and without relief, and harried by Xi raids, he withdrew twenty thousand men, crossed the sea to seize Qingzhou, and Pinglu was lost.

sentences.zh: 肅宗因以希逸為平盧、淄青節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong thereupon made Xiyi Military Governor of Pinglu and Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong then made him military governor of Pinglu and Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 自是淄青常以平盧冠使。

translations.literal: From this time Ziqing often placed Pinglu at the head of the commissioner's title.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Ziqing commission usually prefixed the Pinglu title.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，與諸軍討平史朝義，加檢校工部尚書，賜實戶，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he joined the various armies in pacifying Shi Chaoyi, was additionally made Acting Minister of Works, granted a substantive household fief, and his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoying he helped crush Shi Chaoyi, was made acting minister of works, granted a substantive fief, and had his portrait hung in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 希逸始得青，治軍務農有狀。

translations.literal: When Xiyi first obtained Qing, he had clear achievements in governing the army and promoting agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took Qingzhou he governed troops and promoted farming with real success.

sentences.zh: 後稍怠肆，好畋獵，佞佛，興廣祠廬，人苦之。

translations.literal: Later he gradually grew lax and dissolute, loved hunting, flattered Buddhism, and raised many shrines and monastic lodges, to the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grew slack, devoted himself to hunting and Buddhist patronage, and built shrines everywhere until the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 夜與巫家野次，李正己因眾怨閉闔不內，遂奔滑州。

translations.literal: One night he lodged in the open country with a shaman's family; Li Zhengji, relying on popular resentment, shut the gates and would not admit him, and he thereupon fled to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: One night he camped in the open with a shaman's household; Li Zhengji, playing on popular anger, shut him out of the city, and he fled to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，檢校尚書右僕射，知省事。

translations.literal: He was recalled, made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and directed routine business.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made acting right vice director in charge of routine business.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，封淮陽郡王。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he was created prince of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，遷司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 781 he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未及拜，卒，年六十二，遺敕其子上還前後實封，贈太保。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the post he died, aged sixty-two; he left instructions that his son return the substantive fiefs granted before and after, and was posthumously made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two before he could take office, directing his son to surrender his substantive fiefs, and was posthumously made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 崔寧，本貝州安平人，後徙衛州。

translations.literal: Cui Ning—Cui Ning was originally a man of Anping in Bei Prefecture and later moved to Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning was originally from Anping in Beizhou and later moved to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 世儒家，而獨喜縱橫事，因落魄，客劍南，以步卒事鮮于仲通。

translations.literal: His family for generations were Confucian scholars, yet he alone delighted in coalition diplomacy; because he was down on his luck he sojourned in Jiannan and served Xianyu Zhongtong as an infantryman.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family were scholars for generations, he favored political stratagems; down on his luck, he wandered into Jiannan and served Xianyu Zhongtong as a foot soldier.

sentences.zh: 又從李宓討雲南，無功，還成都，行軍司馬崔論悅之，薦為牙將。

translations.literal: He again followed Li Mi in campaigning against Yunnan without achievement, returned to Chengdu, and Military Affairs Secretary Cui Lun was pleased with him and recommended him as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Mi's failed Yunnan campaign, returned to Chengdu, won the favor of military secretary Cui Lun, and was made a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 歷事崔圓、裴冕。

translations.literal: He successively served Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn under Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.

sentences.zh: 冕被謗，朝廷疑之，遣使者問狀，寧部兵剺耳白其冤，使者以聞。

translations.literal: Mian was slandered and the court suspected him; an envoy was sent to inquire into the matter; Ning's troops pressed forward and plainly declared his innocence, and the envoy reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Mian was slandered and the court grew suspicious, an envoy was sent to investigate; Ning's soldiers intercepted him and forcefully proclaimed Pei's innocence, and the envoy reported back.

sentences.zh: 寧亦還京師，留為折沖郎將。

translations.literal: Ning also returned to the capital and was retained as a Colonel of the Resolute Assault.
translations.idiomatic: Ning too returned to the capital and was kept on as a resolute-assault colonel.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，蜀亂，山賊乘險，道不通。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying Shu was in turmoil; mountain bandits exploited the terrain and roads were impassable.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoying, with Shu in turmoil, mountain bandits held the passes and cut the roads.

sentences.zh: 嚴武白寧為利州刺史，既至，賊遁去，由是知名。

translations.literal: Yan Wu petitioned that Ning be made Administrator of Li Prefecture; once he arrived the bandits fled, and thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu recommended Ning for prefect of Lizhou; on his arrival the bandits dispersed, and he won a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 及武為劍南節度使，過州，心欲與俱西，而利非所屬，使寧自為計。

translations.literal: When Wu became Military Governor of Jiannan he passed through the prefecture and wished in his heart to take him west together, but Li was not under his jurisdiction, so he had Ning devise his own plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu became military governor of Jiannan and passed through Lizhou, he wanted Ning to accompany him west, but Lizhou lay outside his circuit, so he told Ning to find his own way.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「節度使張獻誠見疑，難輒去。

translations.literal: Ning said: "Military Governor Zhang Xiancheng is suspicious of me and it would be hard to leave abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, "Governor Zhang Xiancheng is suspicious of me, so I cannot simply leave.

sentences.zh: 然獻誠嗜利，若厚賂之，寧可以從大夫矣。」

translations.literal: Yet Xiancheng is greedy for profit; if he is richly bribed, I can follow the great officer.
translations.idiomatic: But he is greedy; bribe him heavily and I can follow you west."

sentences.zh: 武然之，以奇錦珍貝遺獻誠，且求寧，獻誠果喜，令自移疾去。

translations.literal: Wu approved this, sent rare silks and precious shells to Xiancheng and also requested Ning; Xiancheng was indeed pleased and ordered him to remove himself on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu agreed, sent rare silks and jewels to Xiancheng and asked for Ning; delighted, Xiancheng let Ning resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 武遂奏為漢州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu thereupon memorialized that he be made Administrator of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu then had him appointed prefect of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃引雜羌寇西山，破柘、靜等州，有詔收復。

translations.literal: Tibetans led various Qiang in raiding the western mountains, broke Zhe and Jing and other prefectures, and an edict ordered recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans led allied Qiang tribes against the western mountains, overran Zhezhou, Jingzhou, and others, and the court ordered their recovery.

sentences.zh: 於是武遣寧將而西，既薄賊城，城皆累石，不得攻，惟東南不合者丈許，諜知之，乃為地道，再宿而拔，拓地數百里。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wu sent Ning to lead troops west; once he drew near the rebel city, the walls were all piled stone and could not be assaulted; only on the southeast was a gap of about a zhang—spies learned this, and he made a tunnel; in two nights he took it and extended territory for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu sent Ning west; the stone-walled rebel stronghold could not be stormed until spies found a one-zhang gap in the southeast; Ning dug a tunnel, took the city in two nights, and extended Tang control for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 虜眾驚相謂曰：「寧，神兵也！」

translations.literal: The barbarian host cried out to one another in alarm: "Ning is divine troops!
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cried in alarm, "Ning commands supernatural troops!"

sentences.zh: 及還，武大悅，裝七寶輿迎入成都，以誇於軍。

translations.literal: When he returned, Wu was greatly pleased, fitted out a seven-jeweled carriage to welcome him into Chengdu, and displayed this to boast before the army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yan Wu was overjoyed, met him in Chengdu with a jeweled carriage, and paraded the honor before the army.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，武卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In 765 Yan Wu died.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬杜濟，別將郭英幹、郭嘉琳皆請英幹之兄英乂為節度使，寧與其軍亦丐大將王崇俊。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Secretary Du Ji, subordinate generals Guo Yinggan and Guo Jialin all requested Yinggan's elder brother Yingyi as Military Governor; Ning and his army also begged for the great general Wang Chongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ji, Guo Yinggan, and Guo Jialin all urged making Yinggan's brother Yingyi governor; Ning's troops asked for Wang Chongjun instead.

sentences.zh: 奏俱至，而朝廷既用英乂矣。

translations.literal: The memorials all arrived, but the court had already appointed Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: All the petitions arrived, but the court had already chosen Yingyi.

sentences.zh: 英乂恨之，始署事即誣殺崇俊，又遣使召寧。

translations.literal: Yingyi resented this; as soon as he took office he framed and killed Chongjun, and again sent envoys to summon Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi resented them; on taking office he framed and killed Chongjun and summoned Ning.

sentences.zh: 寧恐，托拒吐蕃，不敢還。

translations.literal: Ning was afraid and pleaded that he was holding off Tibet and dared not return.
translations.idiomatic: Ning, afraid, claimed he was holding the frontier against Tibet and refused to return.

sentences.zh: 英乂怒，因出兵，聲言助寧，實欲襲取之，即徙寧家於成都，而淫其妾媵。

translations.literal: Yingyi was angry and therefore marched out his army, declaring publicly that he would aid Ning while in fact intending to seize him; he moved Ning's family to Chengdu and violated his concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yingyi marched out, claiming to aid Ning while planning to destroy him, moved Ning's family to Chengdu, and violated his concubines.

sentences.zh: 寧懼，益負阻。

translations.literal: Ning was afraid and became all the more defiant in his stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Ning grew more fearful and entrenched himself.

sentences.zh: 英乂乃自將討之，會天大雪，馬多凍死，士心離，遂敗歸。

translations.literal: Yingyi thereupon personally led a campaign against him; it happened that heaven sent great snow, many horses froze to death, the troops' hearts scattered, and he was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi led the campaign himself, but a blizzard killed many horses, the army fell apart, and he retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 寧聞英乂損裁將卒稟賜，下皆恨怒，又毀玄宗冶金像，乃令軍中曰：「英乂反，輒居先帝舊宮。」

translations.literal: Ning heard that Yingyi had cut the rations and rewards of officers and soldiers, so that all below hated and were angry, and that he had destroyed an image of Emperor Xuanzong casting metal; he therefore told the army: "Yingyi has rebelled and rashly occupies the former emperor's old palace.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yingyi had cut pay and rations, angering the troops, and had destroyed a statue of Xuanzong, Ning told the army, "Yingyi has rebelled and seized the former emperor's palace."

sentences.zh: 乃進薄成都。

translations.literal: He then advanced and pressed close to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 英乂陣城西，使柏茂琳為前軍，英幹為左軍，嘉琳為後軍，與寧戰，茂琳等敗，軍多降寧。

translations.literal: Yingyi formed battle lines west of the city, made Bai Maolin the vanguard, Yinggan the left wing, and Jialin the rear, and fought Ning; Maolin and the others were defeated and many in the army surrendered to Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi drew up west of the city with Maolin in front, Yinggan on the left, and Jialin in reserve; defeated, much of his army went over to Ning.

sentences.zh: 寧即署降將，使率兵還攻，英乂不勝，走靈池，為韓澄所殺。

translations.literal: Ning immediately commissioned the surrendered generals and had them lead troops back in attack; Yingyi could not prevail, fled to Lingchi, and was killed by Han Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ning commissioned the defectors to counterattack; Yingyi was beaten, fled to Lingchi, and was killed by Han Cheng.

sentences.zh: 於是劍南大擾，楊子琳起瀘州，與邛州柏貞節連和討寧。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiannan was greatly disturbed; Yang Zilin rose from Lu Prefecture and joined with Bai Zhenjie of Qiong Prefecture to campaign against Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan fell into chaos as Yang Zilin rose in Luzhou and joined Bai Zhenjie of Qiongzhou against Ning.

sentences.zh: 明年，代宗詔宰相杜鴻漸為山西劍南邛南等道副元帥、劍南西川節度使，往平其亂。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Daizong ordered the chief minister Du Hongjian to be Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the circuits of Shanxi, Jiannan, Qiongnan, and others, and Military Governor of Jiannan West, to go and pacify the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Daizong appointed chief minister Du Hongjian deputy commander over the western circuits and military governor of Jiannan West to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸出駱谷，或進計曰：「公不如駐閬中，數騰書陳英乂罪，嘉寧方略，因以寧所署刺史即授之，使不疑。

translations.literal: Hongjian emerged from Luo Valley; someone offered a plan saying: "Your Lordship would do better to halt at Langzhong, repeatedly send documents setting forth Yingyi's crimes and praising Ning's strategy, and thereupon confirm the prefects Ning has appointed so that he will not be suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Luo Valley, an adviser urged, "Hold at Langzhong, denounce Yingyi in repeated memorials, praise Ning's strategy, and confirm the prefects he has appointed so he will trust you.

sentences.zh: 而後與東川張獻誠及諸帥合兵擾寧，不一年，寧勢且窮，必束身歸命。」

translations.literal: Afterward join with Zhang Xiancheng of East River and the various commanders to combine forces and harass Ning; within a year Ning's power will be exhausted and he is sure to bind himself and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Then join Zhang Xiancheng of East River and the other commanders to harry him; within a year Ning will be cornered and must submit."

sentences.zh: 鴻漸疑未決。

translations.literal: Hongjian hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian wavered.

sentences.zh: 會寧遣使至，獻繒錦數萬，辭卑約甚，鴻漸貪其利，遂入成都，政事一委寧，日與僚屬杜亞、楊炎縱酒高會。

translations.literal: It happened that Ning sent envoys who presented tens of thousands in silk brocade with very humble and submissive words; Hongjian was greedy for the profit, entered Chengdu, entrusted all administration to Ning, and daily with subordinates Du Ya and Yang Yan indulged in wine at grand gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning sent envoys with lavish silks and abject words, Du Hongjian's greed drew him into Chengdu; he handed all affairs to Ning and spent his days feasting with Du Ya and Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 乃表貞節為邛州刺史，子琳為瀘州刺史，以和解之。

translations.literal: He then memorialized Zhenjie as Administrator of Qiong Prefecture and Zilin as Administrator of Lu Prefecture to make peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Zhenjie as prefect of Qiongzhou and Zilin as prefect of Luzhou to settle the feud.

sentences.zh: 又數薦寧於朝。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly recommended Ning at court.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly recommended Ning at court.

sentences.zh: 先是，寧與張獻誠戰，奪其旌節，不肯與，故朝廷因授寧成都尹、西山防禦使、西川節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ning had fought Zhang Xiancheng, seized his insignia of command, and refused to return them; therefore the court accordingly appointed Ning Mayor of Chengdu, Defense Commissioner of the Western Mountains, and Military Affairs Secretary of the West River Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ning had fought Zhang Xiancheng and kept his command insignia, so the court made him mayor of Chengdu, western-mountain defense commissioner, and military secretary of West River.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸既還朝，遂為節度使。

translations.literal: Once Hongjian had returned to court, Ning thereupon became Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Hongjian returned to court, Ning became military governor.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年來朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 768 he came to court.

sentences.zh: 寧本名旰，至是賜名。

translations.literal: Ning's original name was Gan; at this time he was granted the name Ning.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Gan; he was now granted the name Ning.

sentences.zh: 楊子琳襲取成都，帝乃還寧於蜀。

translations.literal: Yang Zilin surprised and seized Chengdu, and the Emperor thereupon returned Ning to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zilin seized Chengdu, the emperor sent Ning back to Shu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，子琳敗。

translations.literal: Before long Zilin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zilin was soon defeated.

sentences.zh: 寧見蜀地險，饒於財，而朝廷不甚有紀，乃痛誅斂；

translations.literal: Ning saw that Shu territory was perilous and rich in wealth, while the court was not very orderly, and therefore levied taxes harshly;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Shu was rugged, wealthy, and poorly governed from afar, Ning taxed it ruthlessly;

sentences.zh: 使弟寬居京師，以賂厚謝權貴，深結元載父子，故寬驟擢御史中丞，寬兄審至給事中。

translations.literal: he had his younger brother Kuan reside in the capital, use bribes to thank the powerful and noble lavishly, and bind himself deeply to Yuan Zai father and son; therefore Kuan was suddenly promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Kuan's elder brother Shen reached Attendant within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: he kept his brother Kuan in the capital to bribe the powerful and court Yuan Zai's faction, so Kuan rose swiftly to vice censor-in-chief and his brother Shen to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 寧在蜀久，兵浸強，而肆侈窮欲，將吏妻妾多為汙逼，朝廷隱忍，不能詰。

translations.literal: Ning was long in Shu, his troops gradually grew strong, and he indulged extravagance to the limit of desire; many officers' and officials' wives and concubines were forced and violated, and the court forbear and could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Long in Shu, his army grew strong while he indulged every excess and forced himself on many officers' wives; the court looked away and dared not call him to account.

sentences.zh: 累加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入朝，進檢校司空、同中書門下平章事，兼山陵使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered court, was advanced to Acting Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Secretariat with Court Session Privileges, and concurrently Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he came to court, was made acting minister of works and chief councilor, and appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb works.

sentences.zh: 俄以平章事為御史大夫，即建白擇御史當出大夫，不宜謀及宰相。

translations.literal: Before long, from chief councilor he became Grand Censor, and immediately proposed that selection of censors should come from the Grand Censor and should not involve consultation with chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made grand censor while retaining his councilorship, he argued that censor appointments should rest with the censorate alone, not with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 因奏李衡、於結等任御史，宰相楊炎怒，寢不行。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Li Heng, Yu Jie, and others be appointed censors; Chief Minister Yang Yan was angry and the proposal was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Li Heng, Yu Jie, and others as censors; Yang Yan blocked the appointments in anger.

sentences.zh: 炎方詆劉晏，寧申救於帝，又素事元載，而炎亦出載門，故銜之，未忍發。

translations.literal: Yan was at that time slandering Liu Yan; Ning pleaded for rescue before the Emperor; he had also long served Yuan Zai, while Yan too came from Zai's faction—therefore Yan harbored resentment but did not yet dare to strike.
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Yan attacked Liu Yan, Ning pleaded for Liu at court; though both men had ties to Yuan Zai's faction, Yan resented Ning and bided his time.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，南蠻與吐蕃合兵入文川、方維、邛郲，覆沒州縣，民逃匿山谷中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year southern barbarians and Tibetans combined forces and entered Wenchuan, Fangwei, and Qiongxi, overthrowing prefectures and counties; the people fled and hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month, southern tribes and Tibetans overran Wenchuan, Fangwei, and Qiongxi, destroying prefectures and counties while the people fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 寧方在朝，軍無帥，德宗促寧進鎮。

translations.literal: Ning was then at court and the army had no commander; Emperor Dezong urged Ning to advance and take up his command.
translations.idiomatic: With Ning at court and Shu leaderless, Dezong pressed him to return to his command.

sentences.zh: 炎業與有嫌，恐已入蜀不可制，即說帝曰：「蜀，天下之奧壤，自寧擅制，朝廷失外府十四年矣。

translations.literal: Yan had long borne a grudge and feared that once he entered Shu he could not be controlled; he thereupon said to the Emperor: "Shu is the hidden fertile land of the realm; since Ning has ruled it on his own, the court has lost this outer province for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, already hostile, feared Ning would become uncontrollable in Shu and told the emperor, "Shu is the empire's richest redoubt; Ning has held it autonomously for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 今寧雖來，以全師守蜀，賦稅入天子者與無地同。

translations.literal: Now though Ning has come, if he guards Shu with his full army, the taxes that enter the Son of Heaven are the same as if there were no territory.
translations.idiomatic: Even now, if he returns with his full army, the court will receive no more revenue than if Shu did not exist.

sentences.zh: 寧本與諸將等夷，獨因叛亂得位，不敢自有，以恩柔煦育，故威令不行。

translations.literal: Ning was originally the equal of other generals and alone gained position through rebellion; he did not dare act on his own authority, and by gentle favor warmed and nurtured them, so his authority and orders did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Ning rose only through rebellion and rules by indulgence rather than authority, so his commands carry no weight.

sentences.zh: 今雖歸之，必無功，是徒遣也；

translations.literal: Even if he is sent back now, he is sure to achieve nothing—this would be dispatch in vain;
translations.idiomatic: Send him back now and he is sure to fail—that would be a wasted dispatch;

sentences.zh: 若其有功，誼不容奪。

translations.literal: if he should have achievement, propriety would not permit taking it away.
translations.idiomatic: and if he succeeds, propriety forbids stripping him of the prize.

sentences.zh: 則西蜀之奧，敗固失之，勝亦非國家所有。

translations.literal: Then the hidden wealth of western Shu—if defeated it is certainly lost, if victorious it is likewise not possessed by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Either way the court loses western Shu: defeat loses it outright, victory leaves it in Ning's hands.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下孰察。」

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should examine this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must weigh this carefully."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿策雲何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What is your plan?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 炎曰：「請無歸寧。

translations.literal: Yan said: "I beg that Ning not be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Do not send Ning back.

sentences.zh: 今朱泚所部范陽勁卒戍近甸，趨與禁兵雜往，舉無不克，因是役得以親兵內其腹中，則蜀將破膽不敢動，然後換授他帥，以收其權，得千里肥饒之地，是謂因小禍受大福也。」

translations.literal: Now the stalwart troops of Fanyang under Zhu Ci garrison the near suburbs; hurry them mixed with the palace guard—nothing undertaken will not succeed; by this campaign we can get trusted troops inside his belly, then Shu will break its courage and not dare move; afterward replace him with another commander to recover his power, and gain a thousand-li of fertile land—this is called receiving great fortune through a small calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's Fanyang veterans garrison the capital approaches; march them with the palace guard and they cannot fail. Use that campaign to plant loyal troops in Ning's rear, terrify Shu into inaction, then replace him and recover a thousand li of rich land—turn a small risk into a great gain."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 遂罷寧西川節度，改兼京畿觀察使、靈州大都督、單於鎮北大都護、朔方節度、鄜坊丹延州都團練觀察等使，托言重臣綏靜北陲，而每道置留後，使得自奏事，杜希全靈州，王翃振武，李建徽鄜州，及戴休顏、杜從政、呂希倩皆炎署置，使伺寧過失。

translations.literal: He thereupon removed Ning from West River military governorship and changed him to concurrent Metropolitan Observation Commissioner, Great Governor of Ling Prefecture, Grand Protector of Shanyu and the North, Military Governor of Shuofang, and Training and Observation Commissioner of the prefectures Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan, on the pretext that a great minister would pacify the northern frontier; yet in each circuit acting commissioners were placed who could memorialize on their own—Du Xiquan at Ling, Wang Hong at Zhenwu, Li Jianhui at Fu, and Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, and Lü Xiqian were all appointed by Yan—to watch for Ning's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was stripped of West River and given nominal commands over the capital region and the northern frontier while Yang Yan installed loyal acting commissioners—Du Xiquan, Wang Hong, Li Jianhui, Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, and Lü Xiqian—to watch his every move.

sentences.zh: 寧至夏州，與希倩招党項，降者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Ning reached Xia Prefecture he joined with Xiqian in summoning the Tangut; those who surrendered were very many.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiazhou, Ning and Lü Xiqian won over many Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 炎惡之，即奏希倩無綏邊才，而以神武將軍時常春代之，更拜寧尚書右僕射、知省事，司空如故。

translations.literal: Yan detested this and immediately memorialized that Xiqian lacked talent to pacify the frontier, and had the Shenwu General Shi Changchun replace him; Ning was further appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs directing routine business, with Minister of Works unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, alarmed, replaced Xiqian with Shi Changchun and recalled Ning as right vice director while leaving his minister of works title intact.

sentences.zh: 朱泚亂，帝出居奉天，寧後數日至，帝喜甚。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled the Emperor went out to reside at Fengtian; Ning arrived several days later and the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled and the emperor fled to Fengtian, Ning arrived a few days later to the emperor's great relief.

sentences.zh: 寧謂所親曰：「上聰明，從善如轉規，但為盧杞所惑至此爾。」

translations.literal: Ning said to those close to him: "The Emperor is intelligent and turns to the good as if revolving a compass, but he has been misled by Lu Qi to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Ning told his intimates, "The emperor is wise and receptive to good counsel, but Lu Qi has led him to this pass."

sentences.zh: 因潸然涕下。

translations.literal: He thereupon shed tears profusely.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he said it.

sentences.zh: 杞聞之，思有以構寧於帝。

translations.literal: When Qi heard of it he thought how he might frame Ning before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qi heard of this and began plotting to destroy Ning.

sentences.zh: 會王翃赴難時，與寧俱出延平門而西，寧數下馬趨廁，輒迂久。

translations.literal: It happened that when Wang Hong went to the rescue he and Ning together went out the Yanping Gate westward; Ning repeatedly dismounted and hurried to the privy, always tarrying long.
translations.idiomatic: During the flight west from Yanping Gate with Wang Hong, Ning kept dismounting for long visits to the privy.

sentences.zh: 翃懼賊追，即呼曰：「既至此，而欲顧望乎？」

translations.literal: Hong, fearing pursuit by rebels, called out: "Having come this far, do you still wish to look back?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing pursuit, Wang Hong shouted, "We've come this far—will you still hang back?"

sentences.zh: 杞微聞，即諷翃以聞。

translations.literal: Qi faintly heard this and prompted Hong to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi overheard and urged Wang Hong to report it.

sentences.zh: 會泚行反間，而除柳渾為宰相，署寧中書令。

translations.literal: It happened that Ci carried out a stratagem of alienation, while Liu Hun was appointed chief minister and Ning was commissioned Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci spread disinformation, Liu Hun was made chief minister, and Ning was named director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時朔方掌書記康湛為盩厔尉，翃逼湛詐作寧遺泚書獻之，杞遂奏：「寧初無效順心，向聞與賊盟署中書令，今果後至，復得所與賊書，反狀明甚。

translations.literal: At that time the Shuofang secretariat clerk Kang Zhan was Assistant Magistrate of Zhouzhi; Hong compelled Zhan to forge a letter from Ning to Ci and presented it; Qi thereupon memorialized: "Ning from the first had no heart of loyal submission; I earlier heard he joined with the rebels in appointing him Director of the Secretariat; now he has indeed arrived late, and again we have obtained the letter he sent the rebels—the signs of rebellion are very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong forced Kang Zhan to forge a letter from Ning to Zhu Ci; Qi then memorialized, "Ning had never been loyal, had long been rumored to have accepted a rebel appointment as director of the Secretariat, had arrived late, and now the forged letter proved treason beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 若兇渠外逼，奸臣內謀，則大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If the vicious ringleader presses from without and treacherous ministers plot within, then the great affair is lost."
translations.idiomatic: With the rebel pressing outside and a traitor within, the dynasty is lost."

sentences.zh: 因俯伏歔欷曰：「臣備位宰相，危不能持，顛不能扶，罪當死。」

translations.literal: He thereupon prostrated himself, sobbing, and said: "Your servant fills the place of chief minister yet in peril could not uphold it, in overturn could not support it—my crime deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, weeping, "I hold the post of chief minister yet could neither steady the throne in peril nor right it in collapse—I deserve death."

sentences.zh: 帝命左右扶起之，乃召寧至朝堂，雲使宣慰江淮。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered attendants to raise him up, then summoned Ning to the court hall on the pretext of sending him to console Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him raised, summoned Ning to court, and pretended to send him to console Jianghuai.

sentences.zh: 俄而中人引寧幕後，使二力士縊殺之，年六十一。

translations.literal: Before long eunuchs led Ning behind the curtain and had two strongmen strangle him to death; he was sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs then led him behind the screen, where two brawny executioners strangled him; he was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 初，命陸贄草制，贄索寧與泚書，將坐其事。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor ordered Lu Zhi to draft the edict; Zhi demanded Ning's letter to Ci, intending to use it to convict him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first ordered Lu Zhi to draft the edict; Lu Zhi asked for Ning's letter to Zhu Ci, intending to use it as evidence.

sentences.zh: 杞復云：「書已亡。」

translations.literal: Qi again said: "The letter is already lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "The letter is already lost."

sentences.zh: 寧死，籍其家，中外冤之。

translations.literal: Ning died, his household property was registered and confiscated, and within and without the court all considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: After Ning's death his property was confiscated, and the whole court regarded it as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 帝乃赦寧親屬，而歸其資雲。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Ning's kin and returned his assets.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned Ning's kin and restored his family's property.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年，寧故將夏綏銀節度使韓潭請以所加禮部尚書雪寧罪，有詔聽其家收葬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, Ning's former officer Han Tan, Military Governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, requested to clear Ning's guilt with the additionally granted post of Minister of Rites; an edict permitted his family to collect the body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In 796, former subordinate Han Tan, military governor of Xia-Sui-Yin, asked to clear Ning's name with the posthumous title of minister of rites, and the court allowed the family to bury him.

sentences.zh: 始，寧入朝，留其弟寬守成都，楊子琳乘間起瀘州，以精騎數千襲據其城。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Ning entered court he left his younger brother Kuan to guard Chengdu; Yang Zilin seized the opportunity to rise from Lu Prefecture and with several thousand elite horsemen surprised and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning went to court he left his brother Kuan in Chengdu; Yang Zilin seized the moment, marched from Luzhou with thousands of elite horsemen, and took the city by surprise.

sentences.zh: 寬戰力屈，寧妾任素驍果，即出家財十萬募勇士，得千人，設部隊，自將以進。

translations.literal: Kuan's strength in battle was exhausted; Ning's concubine Ren Su was bold and resolute, and immediately contributed one hundred thousand in family wealth to recruit brave men, obtained a thousand, organized them into units, and personally led them forward.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was beaten back, but Ning's concubine Ren Su, bold and capable, spent one hundred thousand cash of her own to raise a thousand warriors, formed them into units, and led the counterattack herself.

sentences.zh: 子琳大懼，會糧盡，且大雨，引舟至廷，乘而去。

translations.literal: Zilin was greatly afraid; it happened that grain was exhausted and there was also heavy rain; he brought boats to the court and rode away on them.
translations.idiomatic: Zilin panicked; his grain ran out, rain poured down, and he boarded boats at the palace court and fled downstream.

sentences.zh: 子琳者，本瀘南賊帥，既降，詔隸劍南節度，屯瀘州，杜鴻漸表為刺史。

translations.literal: Zilin had originally been a bandit chief south of Lu; once he surrendered, an edict placed him under the Jiannan Military Governor, garrisoned at Lu Prefecture, and Du Hongjian memorialized him as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zilin had been a southern bandit chief; after surrendering he was placed under Jiannan command, stationed at Luzhou, and Du Hongjian had him appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 既敗，收餘兵沿江而下，諸刺史震栗，備餼牢以饗士。

translations.literal: Once defeated, he gathered his remaining troops and went downriver; the various prefects trembled with fear and prepared provisions and livestock to feast his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he gathered his remnants and sailed downriver; terrified prefects stocked food and livestock to feed his men.

sentences.zh: 過黃草峽，守捉使王守仙伏兵五百，子琳前驅至，悉禽之，遂入夔州，殺別駕張忠，城守以請罪。

translations.literal: Passing Huangcao Gorge, Defense Commissioner Wang Shouxian ambushed with five hundred men; when Zilin's vanguard arrived they were all captured; he then entered Qian Prefecture, killed Vice Prefect Zhang Zhong, and held the city to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangcao Gorge, Wang Shouxian ambushed his vanguard with five hundred men, seized them all, entered Qianzhou, killed vice prefect Zhang Zhong, and held the city to plead for pardon.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其本謀近忠，故授峽州刺史，移澧州鎮遏使。

translations.literal: The court because his original plot had been close to loyalty therefore appointed him Administrator of Xia Prefecture and transferred him to be Suppression Commissioner at Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because his revolt had begun near loyal territory, the court made him prefect of Xiazhou and then suppression commissioner at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 後歸朝，賜名猷。

translations.literal: Later he returned to court and was granted the name You.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to court and was granted the name You.

sentences.zh: 寧季弟密，密子繪，俱以文辭稱。

translations.literal: Ning's youngest younger brother Mi, and Mi's son Hui, were both famed for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's youngest brother Mi and Mi's son Hui were both noted for their literary talent.

sentences.zh: 繪四子：蠡、黯、確、顏，皆擢進士第。

translations.literal: Hui's four sons—Li, An, Que, and Yan—all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's four sons—Li, An, Que, and Yan—all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 蠡字越卿，開成中為戶部侍郎，白罷忌日百官行香，有詔褒可。

translations.literal: Li, style name Yueqing, in the Kaicheng era was Vice Minister of Revenue; he petitioned to abolish the practice of all officials offering incense on taboo days, and an edict praised and approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yueqing served as vice minister of revenue under Kaicheng and successfully petitioned to end the practice of court-wide incense offerings on taboo days, winning imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 歷平盧、天平軍節度使，終尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Military Governor of Pinglu and Tianping armies and ended as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Pinglu and Tianping and ended as left assistant director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子蕘，字野夫，乾符中為吏部侍郎，美文辭，談辯華給，以銓管非所長，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: His son Rao, style name Yefu, in the Qianfu era was Vice Minister of Personnel; skilled in literary composition and brilliant in debate, but because selection and appointment were not his strength he was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rao Yefu, vice minister of personnel under Qianfu, was gifted in letters and eloquent debate but poor at personnel selection, and was sent out as observer of Shanzhou and Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 是時王仙芝亂漢上，河南群盜興，蕘簡侻不曉事，但以器韻自高，委政廝豎，不恤人疾苦。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xianzhi rebelled in the Han region and bandits rose throughout Henan; Rao was simple and crude and did not understand affairs, but held himself high by manner and bearing alone, entrusted government to menials, and did not care for the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Xianzhi ravaged the Han River region and Henan swarmed with bandits, Rao was shallow and incompetent, prized only his own air of refinement, left affairs to lackeys, and ignored the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 或訴旱者，指廷樹示之曰：「柯葉尚爾，何旱為？」

translations.literal: When someone complained of drought he pointed to the courtyard trees and showed them, saying: "The branches and leaves are still like this—what drought is there?
translations.idiomatic: When petitioners complained of drought, he pointed to the courtyard trees and said, "The leaves are still green—what drought?"

sentences.zh: 即搒笞之，上下離心。

translations.literal: He immediately had them beaten with the cudgel, and above and below lost heart for him.
translations.idiomatic: He had them beaten on the spot, and his officers and people turned against him.

sentences.zh: 俄為軍吏所執，髡其髯鬢。

translations.literal: Before long he was seized by military officers, who shaved off his beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his own officers seized him and shaved off his beard.

sentences.zh: 蕘再拜祈免，乃得去。

translations.literal: Rao bowed twice and begged to be spared, and only then was he allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Rao bowed repeatedly for mercy and was finally allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 渴甚，求飲於民，民飲以溺。

translations.literal: Extremely thirsty, he begged drink from the people, and the people gave him urine to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Parched with thirst, he begged water from the people, and they gave him urine to drink.

sentences.zh: 坐失守，貶端州司馬，終左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On account of losing his post he was demoted to Military Adjutant of Duan Prefecture and ended as Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For losing his command he was demoted to staff officer at Duanzhou and ended as left attendant of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 黯，字直卿，開成初為監察御史，奏郊廟祭事不虔。

translations.literal: An, style name Zhiqing, at the beginning of Kaicheng was Investigating Censor and memorialized that suburban and ancestral temple sacrifices were not performed with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhiqing, early in Kaicheng, served as investigating censor and reported negligent suburban and ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 文宗語宰相曰：「宗廟之禮，朕當親之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong told the chief ministers: "The rites of the ancestral temple—I ought to perform them in person.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong told his chief ministers, "The ancestral rites ought to be performed by me in person.

sentences.zh: 但千乘萬騎，國用不給，故使有司侍祠，然是日朕正衣冠坐以俟旦。

translations.literal: But with a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen the state expenditures cannot suffice, so I have the responsible offices attend the sacrifices; yet on that day I dress properly and sit waiting for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: But with a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders the treasury cannot bear it, so the responsible offices attend in my stead—yet on those days I dress properly and sit waiting for dawn.

sentences.zh: 今聞主者不虔，祭器敝惡，豈朕事神蠲絜意邪？

translations.literal: Now I hear the officiants are not reverent and the sacrificial vessels are worn and foul—is this my mind of pure purification in serving the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear the officiants are irreverent and the vessels shabby—is that how I mean to honor the spirits?

sentences.zh: 公宜敕有司道朕斯意。」

translations.literal: You ought to order the responsible offices to convey this intention of mine.
translations.idiomatic: You should instruct the responsible offices to convey my meaning."

sentences.zh: 黯乃具條以聞。

translations.literal: An thereupon set forth the items in detail and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: An then laid out the details in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 擢員外郎，累遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outside Affairs Officer and successively advanced to Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outside affairs officer and eventually to remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 確、顏，位皆郎中。

translations.literal: Que and Yan both held posts as Court Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Que and Yan both rose to court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 嚴礪，字元明，震從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Yan Li—Yan Li, style name Yuanming, was the younger cousin of Yan Zhen on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li, style name Yuanming, was a paternal cousin of Yan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 少為浮屠法，太守見之，偉其材，表為玄武尉。

translations.literal: In youth he practiced the Buddhist law; the prefect saw him, admired his talent, and recommended him as Captain of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied Buddhism; the prefect admired his ability and recommended him as captain of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 震在山南，署牙將。

translations.literal: When Zhen was in Shannan he appointed him a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhen served in Shannan he made Li a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 德宗之幸，主饋餉有功。

translations.literal: During Dezong's flight to safety he supervised provisions and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Dezong's flight from Chang'an he distinguished himself managing supplies.

sentences.zh: 然輕躁多奸謀，以便佞自將。

translations.literal: Yet he was frivolous and rash with many treacherous schemes, and relied on flattery to conduct himself.
translations.idiomatic: But he was rash, scheming, and prided himself on sycophantic cleverness.

sentences.zh: 累為興州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly made Administrator of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 震卒，以礪權主留府事，遺言薦之，即拜本道節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, Li was placed in charge of acting commissioner of the remaining prefectural affairs; Zhen's dying words recommended him, and he was immediately appointed Military Governor of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhen died, Li took charge of the headquarters; on Zhen's deathbed recommendation he was immediately made military governor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔下諫議大夫、給事中、補闕、拾遺合議，皆以為「礪資淺，士望輕，不宜授節制」，帝不從。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for Remonstrance Grand Masters, Attendants within the Palace, Supplements, and Reminders to deliberate jointly; all considered that "Li's qualifications are shallow and the esteem of scholars is light—he should not be granted military commission," but the Emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered remonstrance officials, attendants, and remembrancers to deliberate; all agreed that "Li was too shallow in qualification and too light in reputation to command a circuit," but the emperor overruled them.

sentences.zh: 礪在位，貪沓茍得，士民不勝其苦。

translations.literal: While Li held office he was greedy, grasping, and opportunistic; scholars and commoners could not bear his suffering inflicted on them.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was greedy and grasping, and the people could not endure his exactions.

sentences.zh: 素惡鳳州刺史馬勛，即誣奏，貶賀州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He had long hated Ma Xun, Administrator of Feng Prefecture, and immediately framed a memorial against him, demoting him to Registrar of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had long hated Fengzhou prefect Ma Xun, framed him in a memorial, and had him demoted to registrar at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 劉辟反，以儲備有素，檢校尚書左僕射，節度東川。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, because his stores and preparations were longstanding he was made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Governor of East River.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, his long-standing stockpiles earned him appointment as acting left vice director and military governor of East River.

sentences.zh: 擅沒吏民田宅百餘所，稅外加斂錢及芻粟數十萬。

translations.literal: He on his own authority confiscated more than a hundred residences and fields of officials and commoners, and beyond the taxes additionally levied money and fodder grain to the number of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He seized more than a hundred properties from officials and commoners and extorted hundreds of thousands in cash and grain beyond regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 809 and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 後監察御史元稹奉使東川，劾發其贓，請加惡謚。

translations.literal: Later Investigating Censor Yuan Zhen, on a mission to East River, impeached and exposed his corruption and requested that a malign posthumous title be added.
translations.idiomatic: Later, investigating censor Yuan Zhen, on mission to East River, exposed his corruption and asked that a demeaning posthumous title be granted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其死，故但追田宅奴婢還其主，稅外所斂悉蠲除云。

translations.literal: The court because he was already dead therefore only pursued recovery of fields, houses, and slaves to return them to their owners, and completely remitted all levies beyond the taxes—thus it ended.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was already dead, the court only ordered his seized lands, houses, and slaves returned to their owners and remitted all extralegal levies.
